grades.quote: the suffixes of the instruction name include `.B` (signed byte), `.H` (signed half word), `.W` (signed word), `.D` (signed double word), `.BU` (unsigned byte)
grades.reason: Explains that the .B suffix means signed byte and .BU means unsigned byte in LoongArch mnemonics. This gives only auxiliary naming context. It does not describe how LD.B and LD.BU extend the loaded value.

grades.quote: `LD.{B/H/W/D}` retrieves the data of one byte/halfword/word/double word from the internal sign extension and writes it into the general register `rd` .
grades.reason: Lists the ld.b and ld.bu formats and says LD.B/H/W/D sign-extend the loaded data into rd. This covers the signed side of the comparison. It does not describe the zero-extension of LD.BU.
This is about the RISC-V Zc cm.push instruction sequence. It is the wrong ISA and does not address LoongArch byte loads.
The LD.B pseudocode shows the loaded byte is sign-extended to GRLEN, so a byte with its top bit set fills the upper bits with 1s. It does not show LD.BU for contrast.
